why.trigger: T6 was the only prediction PRED-005 got wrong, and it failed in a direction that matters. I predicted the onset of large-job harm is a pure function of m/N. It is not: at every matched ratio, N=128 had a LOWER flow balance than N=64, and the gap widened with the ratio (0.011 at m/N=0.5, 0.154 at m/N=1.0).
why.stake: E6 measured r_safe = 0.75 at N=64. Philly's worst real virtual cluster sits at m/N = 0.59 with a pool of 217 GPUs -- more than three times larger than the N I measured at. If r_safe falls with N, the 0.59 that looked comfortably safe at N=64 may not be safe at N=217. This decides whether EP-0004's demotion was correctly calibrated or too generous to the real trace.

E7.design: same as E6: small-job background (theta=0.4 geometric shape over needs 1..N/2) plus one large class at need = m arriving with probability p_m. Sweep m/N and N jointly.
E7.seeds: 5 seeds for N <= 128, 3 seeds for N >= 256 (cost)
E7.r_safe_definition: the largest tested ratio at which the m class keeps flow balance >= 0.9, same definition as E6

detector: unchanged from PRED-003/PRED-005: unusable / class-starved (spread > 0.30) / stable (min flow balance >= 0.995) / otherwise the 30k-vs-120k horizon test. r_safe uses the m class's own flow-balance threshold of 0.9, as in E6.

predictions.claim: r_safe falls monotonically with pool size
predictions.criterion: r_safe(32) >= r_safe(64) >= r_safe(128) >= r_safe(256) >= r_safe(512), allowing equality

predictions.claim: the fall is material, not marginal: at N=512 the safe ratio is at least one grid step below the N=64 value
DECIDING. At Philly's real ratio and a realistic pool size the class is still fed: at N=256, m/N = 0.625 (the grid point just above Philly's 0.59), greedy SRPT keeps flow balance >= 0.9
predictions.falsified_if: below 0.9, which would mean EP-0004's demotion was too generous and Philly's 11cb48 VC is in fact inside the harmful region
predictions.note: I expect this to pass, which again is the outcome unfavourable to my own earlier claim's practical relevance

predictions.claim: at m = N the whole-pool class gets worse with pool size
predictions.criterion: flow balance(m=N) decreases monotonically in N over {64, 128, 256}

predictions.claim: EASY backfill is insensitive to pool size as well as to ratio
predictions.criterion: flow balance(easy_backfill) >= 0.99 at every N and every ratio

predictions.claim: at a fixed ratio the large class's mean JCT grows with N
the ratio still dominates the pool size: across the tested box, moving the ratio from 0.5 to 1.0 at fixed N changes flow balance more than moving N from 32 to 512 at fixed ratio
predictions.criterion: max over N of [fb(r=0.5) - fb(r=1.0)] > max over r of [fb(N=32) - fb(N=512)]
predictions.falsified_if: the pool-size effect is the larger one

predictions.claim: small pools are more forgiving: at N=32 the class survives a ratio that N=64 does not

pre_committed_consequence.if_U3_passes: EP-0004's demotion stands as written. Current Understanding replaces the single number 0.75 with a pool-size-dependent band, and the practical guidance becomes 'compare your largest job to your pool capacity, and use a stricter ratio for larger pools'.
pre_committed_consequence.if_U3_fails: The demotion in EP-0004 was too generous. Philly's 11cb48 virtual cluster is inside the harmful region at its real scale, the practical claim is reinstated for pools of a few hundred GPUs, and the headline goes back to naming a real production configuration.

declared_unknowns: whether the N-dependence saturates or keeps falling beyond 512

whether it is really pool size or the number of background job classes (which grows with log N in this mix family) that drives the effect -- these are confounded by construction here and separating them needs a fixed-class-count control
whether the effect survives a non-exponential service distribution
